name: Continue
tagline: An AI coding assistant with editor integrations and a command-line agent.
hook: A focused CLI guide to authentication, terminal interfaces, tools, hooks, configuration precedence, exit codes, and tests.
summary: Continue's analyzed file applies only to extensions/cli. It maps authentication, terminal interfaces, tools, and hooks, then gives the TypeScript CLI's build and test rules.

techniques.title: Make layered hook configuration explicit
techniques.body: The hooks section lists user-global, project, and project-local settings in increasing precedence. Agents can inspect the correct layer instead of assuming the first configuration file controls behavior.

techniques.title: Define the protocol meaning of exit codes
techniques.body: The guide distinguishes a blocked operation from an error that should not block it. It also states how stderr becomes feedback when a hook rejects an action.
techniques.quote: - **Exit code semantics**: 0 = proceed, 2 = block (stderr becomes feedback), other = non-blocking error

techniques.title: Name unsupported hook types
techniques.body: The hook inventory separates implemented command and HTTP handlers from prompt and agent handlers that are not implemented. This keeps a familiar configuration name from being mistaken for a supported feature.

techniques.title: Show the import spelling required by the build
techniques.body: The build section connects the package's module setup with explicit file extensions. A short contrasting example gives an agent the syntax needed for relative imports.
techniques.quote: - Relative import paths require explicit file extensions, e.g. 'from "./test.js"' instead of 'from "./test"'

steal: List configuration layers in precedence order.
Document the meaning of control-flow exit codes.
Mark recognized but unimplemented capabilities explicitly.
Pair module-system requirements with an exact import example.
